cases.question: what is the Brannock Lantern Walk
cases.passage: The Brannock Lantern Walk is an evening procession of paper lanterns held each November in the market town of Brannock. It was first organised in 1931 by the parish bell ringers. Around 4,000 people now take part, and the route runs for about two miles along the river. The walk ends with a bonfire on Copse Hill.
cases.quote: an evening procession of paper lanterns
cases.looking_for: a description of what the event is

cases.question: where is the Otterfold Hiring Fair held
cases.passage: The Otterfold Hiring Fair is an annual livestock and trade fair held on the common at Otterfold in the Velling valley. It dates from a charter granted in 1408 that allowed farm workers to seek new employers each Michaelmas. The modern fair is run by a volunteer committee of twelve. Its best known event is the shearing contest, won in recent years by Corran Bleddyn.
cases.quote: held on the common at Otterfold
cases.looking_for: the place where the fair is held

cases.question: what kind of race is the Gullmouth Tray Race
cases.passage: The Gullmouth Tray Race is a running race in which waiters carry a tray holding a full glass and a bottle along the harbour wall. Competitors must finish with nothing spilled, or they receive a time penalty of thirty seconds. The race was started in 1977 by the owners of the Anchor Rooms hotel. The fastest time on record is 2 minutes 41 seconds.
cases.quote: waiters carry a tray holding a full glass
cases.looking_for: the type of race it is

cases.question: what month is the Kestwick Apple Wassail
cases.passage: The Kestwick Apple Wassail is a midwinter orchard custom held every January in the cider villages around Kestwick. Participants sing to the oldest tree in each orchard and pour cider on its roots to wish for a good harvest. The custom was revived in 1964 after a gap of nearly forty years. Its present organiser is the Kestwick Orchard Trust.
cases.looking_for: the month the wassail takes place

cases.question: what is the Saltreach Kite Festival
cases.passage: The Saltreach Kite Festival is a two-day gathering of kite flyers on the dunes north of Saltreach, held on the last weekend of August. It began in 1989 as a club meeting of eleven members. The festival now draws teams from more than twenty countries. The largest kite flown there, a ray named Big Mabel, measured 38 metres across.
cases.quote: a two-day gathering of kite flyers
cases.looking_for: what the festival is

cases.question: how often is the Dunmarrow Tattoo held
cases.passage: The Dunmarrow Tattoo is a military music and pageant event staged every second summer on the castle esplanade at Dunmarrow. Each performance runs for about ninety minutes and ends with a lone piper on the battlements. The first tattoo, in 1952, raised money for a veterans' hospital. Its producer since 2018 has been Ailsa Rennick.
cases.looking_for: how often the tattoo takes place

cases.question: what is the Varnholm Midnight Regatta
cases.passage: The Varnholm Midnight Regatta is a sailing race around the islands of the Varnholm archipelago, starting at eleven at night on midsummer's eve. Boats must round six marker buoys and return to the harbour at Lissvik. The course is about 34 nautical miles long. The regatta was founded in 1923 by the Lissvik Sailing Society, and the winning crew receives the Silver Gull trophy.
cases.quote: a sailing race around the islands
cases.looking_for: a description of the regatta

cases.question: what is raced at the Penhallow Goose Fair
cases.passage: The Penhallow Goose Fair is an autumn fair in Penhallow whose main event is a race of geese along the high street. It was first recorded in 1587, when it was chiefly a market for selling birds before winter. Today the fair also has a funfair and a ploughing match. Around 15,000 visitors attend over its three days.
cases.quote: a race of geese along the high street
cases.looking_for: the animal that is raced

cases.question: what is the Morrowdene Book Festival
cases.passage: The Morrowdene Book Festival is a ten-day literary festival held each spring in the spa town of Morrowdene. Its programme includes about 300 readings, talks and workshops. The festival was founded in 1994 by the bookseller Hester Quayle. Its director since 2020 has been Tobias Fenwright.
cases.looking_for: a description of the festival

cases.question: how long is the Crane Fell Horseshoe race
cases.passage: The Crane Fell Horseshoe is a 23-mile fell race over the eleven summits that ring the Crane Fell valley. It climbs a total of about 2,400 metres. The race was first run in 1962 by four members of the Crane Fell climbing club. The men's record of 3 hours 12 minutes was set by Davey Ashburn in 1988.
cases.looking_for: the distance of the race

cases.question: when is the Thimbleby Onion Fair
cases.passage: The Thimbleby Onion Fair is a street market held on the first Monday of October in the cathedral city of Thimbleby. Growers from the surrounding marsh villages sell plaited strings of onions from stalls along Castle Lane. The fair was first held in 1316. Attendance in recent years has been around 30,000.
cases.looking_for: the date the fair is held

cases.question: how heavy is the stone in the Wendlecombe Stone Chase
cases.passage: The Wendlecombe Stone Chase is a cross-country foot race in which runners carry a stone weighing 20 kilograms from the quarry at Holloway Top to the village green. The race is run every Easter Monday and covers about three miles. It was first recorded in 1823. The current record holder is Fergus Tull, who finished in 19 minutes in 2014.
cases.looking_for: the weight of the stone carried

cases.question: what is the Pellingford Mop
cases.passage: The Pellingford Mop is a street fair held for three days each October in the centre of Pellingford. It began as a hiring fair where servants seeking work carried a mop or other sign of their trade. Today it is mainly a funfair, with around 120 rides and stalls. The fair is opened each year by the mayor reading the charter of 1554.
cases.quote: a street fair held for three days each October
cases.looking_for: what the mop is

cases.question: what day is the Mellbury Pancake Dash run
cases.passage: The Mellbury Pancake Dash is a race run on Shrove Tuesday by women of the parish, each tossing a pancake in a frying pan as she runs. The course runs 380 metres from the market cross to the church porch. The earliest record of the race dates from 1611. The winner receives a prayer book from the vicar.
cases.looking_for: the day the race is run

cases.question: what does the Carrow Haven Herring Festival celebrate
cases.passage: The Carrow Haven Herring Festival is a harbour festival celebrating the town's fishing history, held over the second weekend of June. It was started in 1985 by the lifeboat crew to raise funds. The main events are a smoked fish market and a rowing race between the old herring drifters. Its patron is the retired skipper Ned Polgrain.
cases.looking_for: what the festival celebrates

cases.question: how long does the Asterby Folk Gathering last
cases.passage: The Asterby Folk Gathering is a five-day festival of traditional music and dance held in late July on farmland outside Asterby. The first gathering, in 1971, had only two hundred people. Attendance now stands at around 18,000. Performers play on six stages, the largest of which is the Barn Stage.
cases.looking_for: how many days the gathering lasts

cases.question: what is raced in the Lindenmoor Bathtub Derby
cases.passage: The Lindenmoor Bathtub Derby is a race of home-made boats built from old bathtubs, held on the Lindenmoor reservoir each Whit Monday. Crews of two paddle a course of 800 metres around three buoys. The event was started in 1969 by the Lindenmoor Round Table. In 2019 the Derby raised £42,000 for local charities.
cases.quote: a race of home-made boats built from old bathtubs
cases.looking_for: the kind of craft that is raced

cases.question: where is the Graydon Hill Climb held
cases.passage: The Graydon Hill Climb is a motor sport event held on a private estate road at Graydon Hall in the Corlan hills. Cars run one at a time against the clock over a course of 1,100 metres. The first meeting took place in 1905. The outright record of 27.4 seconds was set in 2012 by Mara Kellaway.
cases.quote: held on a private estate road at Graydon Hall
cases.looking_for: the place where the hill climb is held

cases.question: how often is the Tamsworth Beating of the Bounds held
cases.passage: The Tamsworth Beating of the Bounds is a parish custom in which people walk the whole boundary of the old parish of Tamsworth every seven years. The walk covers about 14 miles and takes a full day. At each boundary stone, the youngest walker is lifted and bumped against it so the place will be remembered. The most recent walk took place in 2023 and was led by the rector, Imogen Strand.
cases.looking_for: how often the custom takes place

cases.question: what is the Corvale Glass Fair
cases.passage: The Corvale Glass Fair is a trade fair for glassmakers and collectors, held each April in the old furnace halls at Corvale. It was first held in 1958, when twelve local works showed their wares. Around 200 exhibitors now take part. The fair's Golden Gather award goes to the best new piece by a maker under thirty.
cases.quote: a trade fair for glassmakers and collectors
cases.looking_for: what kind of fair it is

cases.question: what time of year is the Ivelstoke Snowdrop Festival
cases.passage: The Ivelstoke Snowdrop Festival is a garden festival held each February, when the snowdrops in the woods of Ivelstoke Abbey are in flower. Visitors follow a marked trail through about 40 acres of woodland. The festival was started in 1997 by the head gardener, Ruth Calloway. It raises money for the upkeep of the abbey ruins.
cases.quote: a garden festival held each February
cases.looking_for: the time of year it is held

cases.question: what is the Quenby Rush Bearing
cases.passage: The Quenby Rush Bearing is a summer church festival in which villagers carry bundles of fresh rushes to lay on the floor of St Aldwyn's church. It is held on the Saturday nearest to 5 August. The custom dates from the time when church floors were bare earth. Children lead the procession carrying rush crosses.
cases.looking_for: what the custom involves

cases.question: how far is the Aldersey Swim
cases.passage: The Aldersey Swim is an open-water race of 4.2 kilometres across Lake Aldersey from Brenton Pier to the boathouse at Cray. It is held on the first Sunday of September, when the water is warmest. The first swim in 1934 had seven entrants, of whom three finished. The fastest crossing on record is 49 minutes 12 seconds.
cases.looking_for: the distance of the swim

cases.question: what is the Hollin Bridge Duck Race
cases.passage: The Hollin Bridge Duck Race is a charity event in which several thousand numbered plastic ducks are released into the Hollin Beck and float about 600 metres downstream. It has been held every Boxing Day since 1981. Each duck is sponsored, and the owner of the first duck to cross the line wins a cash prize. In 2022 a record 9,400 ducks were entered.
cases.looking_for: what the duck race is

cases.question: who organises the Ravelsham Show
cases.passage: The Ravelsham Show is an agricultural show organised by the Ravelsham and District Farmers' Club, held each July at Coldharbour Park. The first show was held in 1847 and was founded by the landowner Sir Edmund Pryce. It features cattle and sheep classes, a dog show and heavy horse displays. Around 25,000 people attend each year.
cases.quote: organised by the Ravelsham and District Farmers' Club
cases.looking_for: the body that organises the show

cases.question: what is Cindervale Ember Night
cases.passage: Cindervale Ember Night is an autumn fire festival in which burning barrels of tar are carried through the streets of Cindervale. It takes place on the first Saturday of November. Each barrel is carried by one man until he can no longer bear the heat, then handed on. The custom is first mentioned in a town record of 1702.
cases.quote: burning barrels of tar are carried
cases.looking_for: a description of the festival

cases.question: where is the Glenharrow Games held
cases.passage: The Glenharrow Games is a Highland games held each August at the Haugh, a riverside meadow below Glenharrow village. Events include tossing the caber, the hill race and piping contests. The games were first held in 1832 under the patronage of the Laird of Corrie. The heaviest caber, known as the Glenharrow Pine, weighs 61 kilograms.
cases.quote: at the Haugh, a riverside meadow
cases.looking_for: the venue of the games

cases.question: what do people chase in the Tollbury Cheese Roll
cases.passage: The Tollbury Cheese Roll is a downhill race in which competitors chase a round of cheese down the steep slope of Tollbury Edge. The cheese is given a one-second head start and can reach speeds of over 60 miles an hour. The race takes place on the late May bank holiday. The first runner to the bottom wins the cheese, which weighs about 4 kilograms.
cases.looking_for: the thing the runners chase

cases.question: what is the Ostery Silver Arrow
cases.passage: The Ostery Silver Arrow is an archery contest held each June on the butts at Ostery Grammar School, the oldest such contest in the county. It was founded in 1673 under the will of a former pupil, Thomas Ostery. Archers shoot at a distance of 100 yards. The winner keeps the silver arrow for a year and adds a medal to its chain.
cases.quote: an archery contest held each June
cases.looking_for: what kind of contest it is

cases.question: where is the Fallowmere Marathon run
cases.passage: The Fallowmere Marathon is a road race run each October through the lanes and villages of the Fallowmere valley. It was first run in 1982 with 312 finishers. The course record of 2 hours 14 minutes is held by Tomas Rydell. About 3,000 runners now take part.
cases.quote: through the lanes and villages of the Fallowmere valley
cases.looking_for: the place where the marathon is run

cases.question: who founded the Brindle Cove Shanty Festival
cases.passage: The Brindle Cove Shanty Festival is a weekend of sea songs held each May in the harbour pubs of Brindle Cove. It was founded in 1999 by the retired trawlerman Joss Penmarrick and his daughter Lowenna. More than sixty groups now perform, singing in the streets as well as the pubs. The festival's present chair is Garth Tremayne.
cases.quote: founded in 1999 by the retired trawlerman Joss Penmarrick
cases.looking_for: the name of the founder

cases.question: when did the Hessleford Carnival start
cases.passage: The Hessleford Carnival is a street parade and fair held over the first weekend of August in Hessleford. It was first held in 1923 to raise money for the town's new cottage hospital. The parade includes about forty decorated floats and five marching bands. In 1975 the carnival moved from the old fairground to Victoria Park.
cases.looking_for: the year the carnival began

cases.question: how many people attend the Wellcross Steam Rally
cases.passage: The Wellcross Steam Rally is a gathering of traction engines, steam rollers and other vintage machinery held each September at Wellcross Farm. It draws around 40,000 visitors over three days. The first rally, in 1966, had only nine engines. The rally is run by the Wellcross Steam Preservation Society, which has some 600 members.
cases.looking_for: the number of visitors

cases.question: who won the Pelham Downs Gold Cup in 2025
cases.passage: The Pelham Downs Gold Cup is a steeplechase run each March over three and a quarter miles at Pelham Downs racecourse. The 2025 running was won by Copper Lantern, ridden by Niamh Garvey. The race was first run in 1904. The most successful horse in its history is Old Trooper, who won it four times.
cases.looking_for: the winner of the 2025 race

cases.question: where is the Harbridge Beer Festival held
cases.passage: The Harbridge Beer Festival is an annual festival of cask ales and ciders run by volunteers from the local brewers' guild. It is held each November in the Corn Exchange in Harbridge. Around 250 beers are served over four days. The first festival, in 1978, was held in a church hall.
cases.quote: held each November in the Corn Exchange
cases.looking_for: the venue of the beer festival

cases.question: who is the director of the Calder Mouth Film Festival
cases.passage: The Calder Mouth Film Festival is an international festival of short films held each October in the seaside town of Calder Mouth. Its director is Priya Lomond, who was appointed in 2021. The festival was founded in 1988 by the film critic Maurice Dahl. Its top prize, the Silver Tern, is awarded to the best film under fifteen minutes.
cases.looking_for: the name of the current director

cases.question: how long is the Norreby Canal Marathon
cases.passage: The Norreby Canal Marathon is a canoe race along the waterway from Norreby to the sea lock at Halsend. The course is 52 miles long and crosses 31 portages where boats must be carried around locks. It was first raced in 1948 by a group of scouts. Crews usually take between 18 and 30 hours.
cases.looking_for: the length of the course

cases.question: when is Tilsey Wake held
cases.passage: Tilsey Wake is a village festival whose origins lie in the feast day of the parish church. It is held on the third Sunday of July and the week that follows. Events include a fancy dress parade, a tug of war and a duck race on the brook. The wake was revived in 1952 after a lapse during the war years.
cases.looking_for: the date the wake is held

cases.question: who organises the Grimsditch Agricultural Show
cases.passage: The Grimsditch Agricultural Show is a one-day county show held each August on the Grimsditch showground. It is organised by the Grimsditch Agricultural Society, a charity founded in 1861. The show's president changes each year and in 2025 was the cattle breeder Hugh Merriman. It attracts around 12,000 visitors.
cases.quote: organised by the Grimsditch Agricultural Society
cases.looking_for: the body that organises the show

cases.question: what is the prize for the Wexley Boat Race
cases.passage: The Wexley Boat Race is a rowing race between the crews of Wexley's two rival grammar schools, rowed each spring on the River Wex. The winning crew receives the Wexley Oar, a carved oak blade first presented in 1887. The course is just over two miles long, from Kings Weir to the town bridge. Northgate School leads the series with 71 wins.
cases.looking_for: the name of the prize

cases.question: how many runners are in the Torrin Coast Half Marathon
cases.passage: The Torrin Coast Half Marathon is a road race along the cliff road between Torrin and the lighthouse at Gannet Head. Each year about 4,500 runners take part, with places allocated by ballot. The race began in 1983 with just 210 finishers. The course record is 1 hour 2 minutes, set in 2016.
cases.looking_for: the number of runners

cases.question: when was the Ashenby Poetry Festival founded
cases.passage: The Ashenby Poetry Festival is a week of readings and workshops held each March in the town of Ashenby. It was founded in 1967 by the poet Clement Varley, who ran it until his death in 1990. The festival awards the Ashenby Prize for a first collection. Its readings take place in the Assembly Rooms and the Quaker meeting house.
cases.looking_for: the year the festival was founded

cases.question: where is the Kelderwick Horse Fair held now
cases.passage: The Kelderwick Fair is a horse fair with a history going back to a charter of 1662. Since 2004 it has been held on Langthwaite Common, two miles outside Kelderwick. Before then the horses were traded in the main street, until the town council closed it to traffic. About 1,200 horses change hands in an average year.
cases.looking_for: the place the fair is held now

cases.question: who is the patron of the Sowerby Moor Sheepdog Trials
cases.passage: The Sowerby Moor Sheepdog Trials are a herding competition held each September on the open fell above Sowerby. The patron of the trials is Lady Annis Holgate, whose family has owned the land since 1820. Handlers and dogs must gather five sheep and drive them through three gates and into a pen. The 2024 trials were won by Rhys Pugh and his dog Fly.
cases.quote: The patron of the trials is Lady Annis Holgate
cases.looking_for: the name of the patron

cases.question: how many stages does the Lowdon Edge Festival have
cases.passage: The Lowdon Edge Festival is a rock and pop festival held over three days in June on farmland near Lowdon. Music is played on seven stages, the largest of which holds 30,000 people. The festival was started in 1996 by the promoter Ray Tennick. Around 70,000 people attend each year.
cases.quote: Music is played on seven stages
cases.looking_for: the number of stages

cases.question: when is the Moorhaven Regatta held
cases.passage: The Moorhaven Regatta is a rowing and sailing regatta held on the estuary at Moorhaven. It takes place over the August bank holiday weekend. The first regatta was held in 1838 to mark a royal coronation. Around 300 boats now compete in more than forty races.
cases.quote: over the August bank holiday weekend
cases.looking_for: the date the regatta is held

cases.question: how old is the Penmarrow Fair
cases.passage: The Penmarrow Fair is a street fair held each October in the cathedral town of Penmarrow. It dates from a royal charter granted in 1214, making it one of the oldest fairs in the county. Today the fair fills the market square with about eighty rides and stalls. It was last cancelled in 1940.
cases.looking_for: the age or founding date of the fair

cases.question: who is the race director of the Gannet Ultra
cases.passage: The Gannet Ultra is a 100-mile trail race around the coast of the Isle of Skerrin. The race director is Morven Achlach, who took over from the founder, Alan Brodie, in 2019. Runners have 36 hours to finish. Fewer than half of the starters usually complete the course.
cases.quote: The race director is Morven Achlach
cases.looking_for: the name of the current race director

cases.question: how many scarecrows are in the Wren Valley Scarecrow Festival
cases.passage: The Wren Valley Scarecrow Festival is a village trail of home-made scarecrows held each May in the six villages of the Wren Valley. In a typical year about 220 scarecrows are entered by households, schools and businesses. Visitors vote for their favourite, and the winner receives the Golden Pitchfork. The festival began in 2003 and has raised more than £150,000 for the village halls.
cases.looking_for: the number of scarecrows entered

cases.question: what is the top prize at the Halsworth Brass Band Contest
cases.passage: The Halsworth Brass Band Contest is a competition for brass bands held each Whit Friday in the streets of Halsworth and the villages around it. The overall winner takes home the Halsworth Shield, a silver trophy first presented in 1884. Bands march between villages and play one test piece at each stop. In 2025 a record 96 bands took part.
cases.looking_for: the name of the top prize

cases.question: who won the first Corrigan Memorial race
cases.passage: The Corrigan Memorial is a cycle road race held each April on the hill roads around Ballykeel. The first race, in 1957, was won by Seamus Doherty of the Ballykeel Wheelers. It is named after the club founder Patrick Corrigan, who died in a road accident in 1955. The course is about 140 kilometres long.
cases.looking_for: the winner of the first race

cases.question: how tall is the maypole at Fernhill May Day
cases.passage: Fernhill May Day is a spring festival held on the village green at Fernhill on the first Monday of May. Its maypole stands 26 metres high and is said to be the tallest in the county. The day begins with the crowning of the May Queen, chosen from the girls of the village school. Morris sides from across the region dance on the green in the afternoon.
cases.looking_for: the height of the maypole

cases.question: who is the music director of the Brackwater Proms
cases.passage: The Brackwater Proms is a summer season of orchestral concerts held in the Winter Gardens at Brackwater. Its music director is Lucan Ferrars, who conducts the first and last nights. Guest conductors lead the other concerts, and in 2025 they included Sigrid Holm and Arturo Belli. The season was first held in 1931.
cases.quote: Its music director is Lucan Ferrars
cases.looking_for: the name of the music director

cases.question: how many days does the Calderly Show last
cases.passage: The Calderly Show is a horticultural show of fruit, flowers and vegetables organised by the Calderly Horticultural Society. It runs for two days at the end of August in the town's drill hall. The heaviest marrow ever shown there weighed 54 kilograms. The society was formed in 1874.
cases.looking_for: the length of the show in days

cases.question: what river is the Sallowford Raft Race on
cases.passage: The Sallowford Raft Race is a charity race of home-built rafts held each June. It is run on the River Sallow over a 5-mile course from Bickton Mill to Sallowford Bridge. Teams are often in fancy dress, and many rafts sink before the finish. The race has raised about £300,000 since it began in 1972.
cases.looking_for: the name of the river

cases.question: how much did the Nettlecombe Fun Run raise in 2024
cases.passage: The Nettlecombe Fun Run is a 5-kilometre charity run held each New Year's Day along the seafront at Nettlecombe. In 2024 it raised £38,500 for the local hospice. Runners traditionally wear fancy dress, and prizes are given for the best costume. The first run, in 1986, had 40 entrants.
cases.looking_for: the amount raised in 2024

cases.question: where do people watch the Garron Point Air Show from
cases.passage: The Garron Point Air Show is a free two-day flying display held each July over the bay at Garron Point. Crowds gather on the promenade and the cliff top at Garron Head to watch the displays. The show began in 1993 as a single display by the local flying club. Around 150,000 people attend over the weekend.
cases.quote: on the promenade and the cliff top at Garron Head
cases.looking_for: the place where spectators watch

cases.question: when were the Harlan Mystery Plays last performed
cases.passage: The Harlan Mystery Plays are a cycle of medieval religious dramas performed on wagons in the streets of Harlan. They have been staged every four years since their revival in 1951, most recently in 2022. About 500 local people take part as actors, musicians and crew. The original plays were suppressed in 1569.
cases.looking_for: the year of the most recent performance

cases.question: what are the teams called in the Wenlow Shrovetide Game
cases.passage: The Wenlow Shrovetide Game is a mass football match played through the streets of Wenlow on Shrove Tuesday and Ash Wednesday. The two teams, the Uppers and the Downers, are made up of whoever was born on each side of the Wenlow Brook. The goals are three miles apart, at the sites of two old mills. The ball is thrown into the crowd at two in the afternoon by a guest of honour.
cases.looking_for: the names of the two teams

cases.question: what is the theme of the 2026 Ellingham Arts Festival
cases.passage: The Ellingham Arts Festival is a fortnight of music, theatre and visual art held each June in Ellingham. The theme of the 2026 festival is Rivers and Crossings, chosen by its artistic director, Saoirse Kane. Earlier themes have included Light in 2024 and Harvest in 2025. The festival was founded in 1979.
cases.looking_for: the theme of the 2026 festival

cases.question: who runs Stannard Fireworks Night
cases.passage: Stannard Fireworks Night is a bonfire and fireworks display held each 5 November on the Stannard recreation ground. It is run by the Stannard Rotary Club, which took it over from the town council in 1991. The bonfire is built over three weeks from donated timber. About 20,000 people watch the display.
cases.quote: run by the Stannard Rotary Club
cases.looking_for: the organisation that runs it

cases.question: how high do runners climb in the Scarth Pike Race
cases.passage: The Scarth Pike Race is a fell race from the village of Ullerby to the summit of Scarth Pike and back. Runners climb about 880 metres to the top in just under three miles. The race has been held at the Ullerby Sports each August since 1880. The record time is 41 minutes 7 seconds.
cases.looking_for: the height of the climb

cases.question: who started the Fernley Wheelbarrow Race
cases.passage: The Fernley Wheelbarrow Race is a pub-to-pub relay in which one team member pushes another in a wheelbarrow through the village of Fernley. It was devised in 1974 by Bert Ollerenshaw, the landlord of the Plough Inn, as a bet with a rival publican. Teams must drink half a pint at each of the seven pubs along the route. The fastest team in the race's history finished in 22 minutes.
cases.looking_for: the person who started the race

cases.question: what does the winner of the Gilderdale Ploughing Match get
cases.passage: The Gilderdale Ploughing Match is a contest of horse and tractor ploughing held each October on a different farm in the Gilderdale parish. The champion ploughman receives the Gilderdale Bell, a brass harness bell that has been passed from winner to winner since 1866. Judges mark the straightness of the furrows, the depth and the finish at the ends. Around sixty ploughmen enter each year.
cases.looking_for: the prize given to the champion

cases.question: where is the Wyndham Bay Sandcastle Contest
cases.passage: The Wyndham Bay Sandcastle Contest is a competition for sand sculptures held each August. It takes place on the north beach at Wyndham Bay at low tide, with entrants given four hours before the sea returns. The winning entry in 2024 was a model of the town's pier. The contest was first held in 1956.
cases.quote: on the north beach at Wyndham Bay
cases.looking_for: the place the contest is held

cases.question: how many balloons take off at the Halsey Balloon Fiesta
cases.passage: The Halsey Balloon Fiesta is a gathering of hot-air balloons held each August in the grounds of Halsey Court. At the dawn mass ascent, around 120 balloons take off together. The fiesta also holds a night glow, in which tethered balloons are lit in time to music. It was first held in 1979 with 27 balloons.
cases.looking_for: the number of balloons in the mass ascent

cases.question: who is the chief arbiter at the Wrentham Chess Congress
cases.passage: The Wrentham Chess Congress is a weekend chess tournament held each January at the Wrentham Town Hall. Its chief arbiter is Dennis Okafor, who has controlled the event since 2011. The congress has five sections, from the Open down to a section for players graded under 1200. The 2025 Open was won by the grandmaster Lena Stroud.
cases.quote: Its chief arbiter is Dennis Okafor
cases.looking_for: the name of the chief arbiter

cases.question: what date is the Porthkellis Blessing of the Waters
cases.passage: The Blessing of the Waters is an Epiphany custom at Porthkellis in which the vicar blesses the harbour and throws a wooden cross into the sea. It takes place on 6 January each year, whatever the weather. Swimmers race to recover the cross, and the finder is said to have good luck for the year. cases.question: when did the Penhale Garland Dance start
cases.passage: The Penhale Garland Dance is a spring festival in which couples dance through the streets, in and out of the houses, to the music of the town band. It is held each year on 8 May, unless that falls on a Sunday or Monday. The dance tune is said to be very old, and was first written down in 1802. The festival is the busiest day of the year in Penhale.
cases.looking_for: the year the dance began

cases.question: who is the race director of the Sorrel Ridge Ultra
cases.passage: The Sorrel Ridge Ultra is a 50-mile trail race along the Sorrel Ridge, held each September. It was created in 2008 by the runner Kit Danvers, who had walked the ridge as a boy. The race has a cut-off of 14 hours, and about 60 percent of starters finish. The 2025 women's race was won by Freya Lund.
cases.looking_for: the name of the current race director

cases.question: how many people marched in the 2025 Glendower Day Parade
cases.passage: The Glendower Day Parade is a procession of bands, dancers and decorated floats held each March in the city of Caerwen. The first parade, in 2004, had about 1,000 marchers. It is organised by the Glendower Day Trust with support from the city council. The route ends at the castle, where a concert is held in the evening.
cases.looking_for: the number of marchers in 2025

cases.question: what does the winner of the Lodsworth Ferret Race get
cases.passage: The Lodsworth Ferret Race is a novelty race in which ferrets run through lengths of drainpipe at the Lodsworth summer fete. Heats are run every half hour through the afternoon, with four ferrets in each. The race was first held in 1983 and is the fete's biggest attraction. In 2019 a ferret named Bandit won six heats in a row.
cases.looking_for: the prize for winning the race

cases.question: how long is the Tamsey Raft Race course
cases.passage: The Tamsey Raft Race is a charity race of home-made rafts held each August bank holiday on the River Tamsey. Teams start at Polkerry Bridge and paddle downstream to the quay at Tamsey Mouth. The race was first held in 1979 and has raised more than £500,000 for the lifeboat service. Rafts must be built from barrels, timber and rope, with no engines allowed.
cases.looking_for: the length of the course

cases.question: who is the patron of the Rookhope Festival
cases.passage: The Rookhope Festival is a weekend of brass band music held each May in the village of Rookhope. It was founded in 1951 by the Rookhope Colliery Band to raise money for new instruments. The festival's president is the band's former conductor, Walter Ibbotson. About thirty bands take part in the contest on the Saturday.
cases.looking_for: the name of the patron

cases.question: how heavy is the caber at the Kilbrannan Games
cases.passage: The Kilbrannan Games is a Highland games held each July on the shore at Kilbrannan. Its caber, known as the Kilbrannan Larch, is just over 6 metres long. The caber was cut from the estate woods in 1979 and has been tossed successfully only fourteen times. Other events include the stone put and the weight over the bar.
cases.looking_for: the weight of the caber

cases.question: who won the Pennock Pie Eating Contest in 2025
cases.passage: The Pennock Pie Eating Contest is held each September at the Pennock Show, and competitors race to eat a meat and potato pie. Contestants may not use their hands, and the pie must be eaten down to the dish. The record time of 23 seconds was set in 2014 by Danny Hollis. The contest raises money for the village school.
cases.looking_for: the winner of the 2025 contest

cases.question: how many people went to the first Tremorna Folk Weekend
cases.passage: The Tremorna Folk Weekend is a festival of folk music and dance held each June in the fishing town of Tremorna. It was first held in 1972 in the back room of the Ship Inn. Today the festival draws about 6,000 visitors and fills every pub in the town. The festival's closing concert is held on the harbour wall.
cases.looking_for: the number of people at the first festival

cases.question: what is the record attendance at the Ashbury Show
cases.passage: The Ashbury Show is an agricultural show held each August on the Ashbury showground. About 20,000 people attend in a typical year. The show was cancelled in 2001 because of an outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease. Its president for 2026 is the dairy farmer Eleanor Brice.
cases.looking_for: the highest attendance ever recorded

cases.question: who started the Castlewood Cider Festival
cases.passage: The Castlewood Cider Festival is a weekend celebration of cider and perry held each October in the orchards of Castlewood Farm. Visitors can watch apples being pressed in a horse-drawn mill. The farm has been owned since 1994 by the Hendry family, who also run a cider shop in the village. More than seventy ciders are on sale.

cases.question: what is the trophy for the Fennby Midsummer Race called
cases.passage: The Fennby Midsummer Race is a 7-mile road race held on the Saturday nearest midsummer's day. Runners finish at the Fennby Arms, where prizes are presented. The race was first run in 1983. The trophy for the winner was donated by the race's first champion, Ken Tasker.
cases.looking_for: the name of the trophy

cases.question: how many stalls are at the Alverstone Christmas Market
cases.passage: The Alverstone Christmas Market is a seasonal market held each December along the high street of Alverstone. It runs over the first two weekends of the month, when the street is closed to traffic. The market raises money for the town's Christmas lights, which cost about £30,000 a year. It was started in 1995 by the Alverstone Chamber of Trade.
cases.looking_for: the number of stalls

cases.question: who is this year's Lord of Misrule at the Wellstead Revel
cases.passage: The Wellstead Twelfth Night Revel is a midwinter festival held each 6 January in the village of Wellstead. It is led by a Lord of Misrule, chosen by drawing a bean from a cake. The custom was revived in 1977 by the Wellstead Morris Men. The first Lord of Misrule of the revival was the blacksmith Tom Fairley.
cases.looking_for: the name of this year's Lord of Misrule

cases.question: what is the course record for the Lochend Hill Race
cases.passage: The Lochend Hill Race is a 5-mile mountain race held each June as part of the Lochend Show. The course climbs to the summit of Ben Corrach and returns by the same path. The 2025 race was won by Calum Fraser in 41 minutes 22 seconds, the fastest time for a decade. About 150 runners took part.
